title: Is this population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. 400 plants were genotyped: 52 BB, 200 Bb and 148 bb. The allele frequency is p(B) = (2 × 52 + 200)/800 = 0.38, so Hardy–Weinberg expects the proportions p² = 0.1444, 2pq = 0.4712 and q² = 0.3844.

Test the fit with one parameter estimated from the data. Give χ² (two decimals), the degrees of freedom and the p-value (four decimals).

In the Workbench: **Chi-square tests**, **Test** *Goodness of fit*, the three counts, **Expected proportions from** *Typed*, the three proportions, and **Parameters estimated from the data** 1.

DegreesOfFreedom.says: Three categories give 3 − 1 = 2, but p was estimated from the same data: subtract one more.

hints: Degrees of freedom = categories − 1 − parameters estimated = 3 − 1 − 1.
